subject: Post-demo econ synthesis — token targets, $/1M, CAC payback split
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Myers <danielle@onemed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo econ synthesis — token targets, $/1M, CAC payback split

Hi Danielle — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick synthesis and a few clarifying asks so we can get a concrete pilot SOW drafted. I captured the call notes into the attached profile but wanted to recap here so we’re aligned.

Summary from demo:
- Primary use: patient intake triage + outbound appointment reminders (2 features).
- Expected monthly active users: 20k in month 1, ramp to 80k by month 6.
- Typical conversation length: ~150 tokens prompt, ~120 tokens response (270 tokens roundtrip).
- Expected average calls per user per month: 3 (mix of triage + reminders).

Immediate asks (please confirm):
1) Target budget range for initial 6 months (ballpark is fine): you mentioned a mid-six-figure annual run rate — can you confirm a monthly / quarterly envelope to aim SOW at?
2) Decision criteria on payback: is finance looking for feature-level CAC payback <= 9 months, or a blended payback for the bundle?
3) Any procurement constraints (PO cadence, required terms) we should plan for on the SOW?

Preliminary unit-econ math (back-of-envelope):
- Tokens/month estimate (M): 20k users * 3 calls * 270 tokens * 1 month = 16,200,000 tokens (16.2M) month 1; scale to ~64.8M at month 6.
- Target unit benchmark: you said ~$1k–$2k per 1M tokens budget range — confirm which end we should optimize for.
- If we price at $1,500 / 1M tokens, inference cost estimate (redwood-managed, optimized) = ~$0.40–0.55 / 1k tokens for this workload (varies by model/quant). That maps to ~ $600–$900 / 1M tokens cost, leaving gross margin to allocate to dev/ops & feature economics.

Feature-level ask: for SOW/ROI we’ll create two scopes: (A) Triage-only (higher token density, higher value per conversion) and (B) Triage + reminders bundle. To make the pilot meaningful, can you confirm target $/feature you want to justify to internal stakeholders (e.g., $/completed triage vs $/appointment reminder)?

Next steps I propose:
- You send any existing token logs or destination volumes (I noticed procurement included an export template — attached csv would help).
- We’ll produce a 2-page unit-econ sheet showing $/1M token sensitivity (range $1k–$2.5k) and CAC payback scenarios (6, 9, 12 months) by feature.
- Schedule internal deep-dive with product + finance (30–45m) next week — I’ll send times.

I attached the token profile template from the call as OneMed_token_profile.csv. Thanks — will wait for the budget cadence and any procurement notes.

Best,
Priyom
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OneMed_token_profile.csv (CSV), call-recording-stub.mp3 (link)

Subject: Re: Post-demo econ synthesis — token targets, $/1M, CAC payback split

Thanks Priyom — great recap and exactly what I expected to see. A few quick answers: 

1) Budget cadence: initial pilot budget is $45k for Q2 (pilot months 1–3), with an expected expansion window if we hit clinical throughput goals. If pilot looks good we have a path to $200–250k for the following 9 months.
2) Payback target: finance will push for <=9 months payback on the triage feature. For non-core features (reminders) they’re OK with blended payback up to 12 months.
3) Procurement: we need a standard Master Services Agreement (our template) + a 60-day SOC2 evidence window. PO on our side requires a signed SOW + vendor W9. 

I attached the token export and a rough SOW outline (see attachments). The token export is sample traffic for the last month of a similar rollout — you can use it for initial projections.

Also: our product lead (not copied) asked whether you can show a $/feature map that ties inference cost to incremental revenue per completed triage. Even a conservative uplift assumption (1–2% downstream revenue capture) will help our CFO sign off.

Will loop in procurement if you send a draft SOW.

—Danielle
Director of Digital Products
OneMed Health

Attachments: OneMed_token_profile.csv, SOW_outline.docx

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Danielle — this is perfect. I pulled the attached draft unit-econ workbook (redwood-unit-econ-proposal.xlsx) and sketched three canonical scenarios so procurement & finance can see sensitivity:

Scenario A — Conservative
- Price: $2,200 / 1M tokens
- Redwood inference estimated cost: $1,100 / 1M tokens (after batching & quantized runtime)
- Gross margin on tokens: $1,100 / 1M
- Example outcome: Month 1 tokens = 16.2M -> platform bill = $35,640; token cost = $17,820; remaining margin covers infra and ops.

Scenario B — Mid (our recommended pilot target)
- Price: $1,500 / 1M tokens
- Cost: $800 / 1M tokens
- Margin: $700 / 1M tokens
- Example outcome: Month 1 bill = $24,300; cost = $12,960; margin = $11,340 to allocate to dev + feature economics.

Scenario C — Aggressive
- Price: $1,000 / 1M tokens
- Cost: $600 / 1M
- Margin: $400 / 1M
- Example outcome: Month 1 bill = $16,200; cost = $9,720; margin = $6,480.

Feature-level mapping (sample using Scenario B mid target):
- Completed triage conversion value (conservative): $45 incremental revenue per completed triage
- Average completed triages/month (pilot): assume 8% completion of triage flows -> 20k users * 3 calls * 0.08 = 4,800 completions -> incremental revenue = $216k/month (gross).
- Inference token bill (month 1, Scenario B): ~$24.3k. If we allocate 40% of token bill to triage feature (higher token density), effective token cost charged to triage = $9.72k.
- $/feature (triage) = token-cost-per-completion = $9.72k / 4,800 ≈ $2.02 per completed triage (inference only).

CAC payback examples (Scenario B):
- If average CAC to acquire a user attributed to the feature = $10, then payback months = CAC / (incremental contribution margin per user). Using conservative uplift and margin assumptions, we can model payback ≈ 6–10 months depending on adoption. We’ll include a table in the workbook showing 6/9/12 month thresholds.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I’ll share the workbook (attached) and a 2-page exec summary for your CFO that shows the $/1M sensitivity + the $/feature rows (triage vs reminders).
2) If Q2 pilot budget of $45k is confirmed, we’ll propose Pilot SOW A (triage-focused, 3 months) priced against Scenario B targets, with an option to extend & discount if rollouts hit throughput gates.
3) Procurement: please send your MSAT + W9 so legal can pre-clear terms. Procurement, happy to take point with your team on SOW specifics.

Can I schedule a 30m call with your product finance lead + our pricing lead Ben on Wed/Thu? I’ll drop times.

Thanks — I’ll update HubSpot and attach the workbook link in the next email.

Best,
Priyom

Attachments: redwood-unit-econ-proposal.xlsx
